# Purābheda Sutta (Snp 4.10 (PTS Snp 166))
**ID:** Snp 4.10 (PTS Snp 166)
**Section:** Suttanipāta (snp)
**Collection:** Suttas-Early-2
**Title (Pali):** Purābheda Sutta
**SuttaCentral:** https://suttacentral.net/snp4.10
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0505m.mul3.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Purābheda Sutta* ("Before the Breakup" or "Discourse Before the Disintegration", also noted as *Purābhedana* in an *uddāna*) is the tenth discourse of the *Aṭṭhakavagga* in the *Suttanipāta* (verses 848–861; PTS Snp 166) [Anderson and Smith 1913; Norman 1997-2001; SuttaCentral; symposium2010]. The sutta opens with a question addressed to Gotama inquiring what kind of vision and moral conduct characterize one who is termed "peaceful" (*upasanta*) [Anderson and Smith 1913]. In reply, the Buddha outlines the attainment of internal peace (*ajjhattasanti*) and the appeasement of dispositions (*sabbasaṅkhārasamatha*) realized before the breakup of the body (*purā bhedā*), explicitly rejecting craving and striving for both becoming (*bhava*) and non-becoming (*vibhava*) [Ruegg and Schmithausen 1990; symposium2010]. Like other discourses in the *Aṭṭhakavagga*, it depicts the perfected practitioner as free from partisan attachments and dogmatic disputes [Steinkellner and Tauscher 1983].
In commentarial accounts preserved in the *Paramatthajotikā*, the discourse is framed as a dialogue with an apparitional Buddha (*nimmita*), at the conclusion of which a multitude of deities attained arahanthood [Tournier et al. 2018]. The sutta was later incorporated into the expanded Burmese *Catubhāṇavārapāḷi* (*Paritta*) tradition [Kalupahana 2001], and has been utilized in modern meditation expositions by Theravāda teachers such as Mahasi Sayadaw and Ven. Dhammajiva, who examines its analysis of anger and craving [de Silva 2017; Dhammissara 2017].
Canonical commentary on the sutta is provided by the *Purābhedasuttaniddesa* in the *Mahāniddesa* (Mnd 10), which DharmaNexus aligns extensively with 62 matching Pali-internal reuse passages (such as §2.1–3.4) [DharmaNexus; SuttaCentral]. A curated Chinese parallel exists as a discourse in the *Arthapada-sūtra* (T 198 佛說義足經) [SuttaCentral; Tournier et al. 2018]. DharmaNexus additionally aligns verses of the sutta with the Sanskrit Patna Dharmapada (§3.2–3.3 matching verses 222–226), as well as several Tibetan Mahāyāna translations, including the *Saddharmānusmṛtyupasthāna* (D0287-3) and the *Gaganagañjaparipṛcchāsūtra* (D0148) [DharmaNexus].
